description: A validation applies to the runtime value it checked, not to every later read of the same field. One request writes a caller-controlled slug into the pages store. Both readers check the same full-string allow-list. The first sends the checked local and is silent. The second reloads the record and reads page.slug again; nothing proves that fresh stored value still satisfies the earlier check, so it must report. The historical failure was in lowering: property reads were cached by base and path, turning both page.slug expressions into one IR value and crediting a sanitizer across the reload.

expected.sourceLabel: the page store, written by POST /pages
expected.note: the allow-list checked an earlier read; reload can replace the stored value before this fresh page.slug reaches markup
